housing.summary: Numbeo reports a crowd-sourced average of €2,271.15 per month for a one-bedroom apartment in Amsterdam city centre (updated 30 August 2026); Pararius is a current Amsterdam rental portal. A deposit norm was not grounded in the cited rent source.

banking.summary: ABN AMRO allows eligible newcomers to open an account with an official Dutch home address and a Dutch ID or international passport; a BSN may be supplied within 120 days.

schools.summary: The I amsterdam directory lists international schools in and around Amsterdam and states that many English-language international schools follow International Baccalaureate programmes.

legal_admin.summary: A newcomer staying longer than four months must register with the municipality in the Personal Records Database (BRP) within five days of arrival.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register as a resident in the BRP with the municipality within 5 days of arrival when staying longer than 4 months.

tax_finance.summary: The municipality issues the citizen service number (BSN) at BRP registration; short-stay non-residents can receive one through RNI registration, and the BSN is used for tax dealings.

transport.summary: IN Amsterdam identifies GVB as Amsterdam's public-transport network. Foreign-licence exchange eligibility depends on BRP registration and country/status; eligible applicants apply at a local City Office. Almost everyone who lives or works in the Netherlands must take standard health insurance and needs a BSN to register. A current monthly-pass price was not established from this source.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: Check eligibility based on country and status; if eligible and registered in the BRP, apply at a local City Office before the foreign licence expires.
transport.healthcare_registration: Obtain a BSN, then register with a health insurer for standard Dutch health insurance.
